newsitem.title: ITALY: Stet to absorb Telecom Italia ahead of sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Stet to absorb Telecom Italia ahead of sell-off.

text.p: Italy's state-controlled telecommunications holding company Stet will absorb telephone operating company Telecom Italia ahead of the privatisation of the sector later this year, the Treasury said on Friday.

The new company, which will continue to control separately listed cellular phone group Telecom Italia Mobile and a number of cable and engineering firms, had combined turnover of some 40 trillion lire ($25.2 billion) in 1996.
The Treasury indicated that the company, which is being created to rationalise operations within the group, would be called Telecom Italia.
Full terms of the merger are expected to be completed between the end of June and the end of August with the much delayed privatisation now scheduled by the end of October.
The Treasury holds just over 60 percent of Stet, which in turn holds 63.4 percent of Telecom Italia.

Italians have dubbed the planned sale of the telecoms sector as the "mother of all privatisations," but the flotation has been regularly delayed in the past and political bickering continues to cast a shadow over the sell-off.

Legislation needed for the sale is blocked in parliament and a key government ally, the hard left Communist Refoundation, has threatened to bring down Prime Minister Romano Prodi's coalition if it presses ahead with the privatisation.
Government officials have held behind-the-scenes meetings with Refoundation, which is ideologically opposed to the sell-off, to try to break the deadlock.
"Italy is risking its credibility with the privatisations over the coming months," said Giorgio Fossa, the head of employers' federation Confindustria.

Ministry sources say the Treasury is determined to stick to its latest timetable and British banking sources say that one of the lead banks, Barclays De Zoete Wedd, has been told by Italy that there can be no further delay to the sale.
The Treasury took control of Stet from state holding company IRI at the start of the year, with ministers widely reported to be unhappy at the way the group was being prepared for privatisation.

The Italian media reported that the Treasury was poised to replace top Stet directors, with Tommaso Tommasi di Vignano, director-general of Telecom Italia, being lined up to take over from Ernesto Pascale as managing director of the merged group.
"I believe that these reports are well founded," said Nerio Nesi, chairman of parliament's industry commission.
Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi held long talks with Pascale on Friday as well as with Stet chairman Biagio Agnes.
La Repubblica newspaper reported that the government planned to replace Agnes with Guido Rossi, a former head of the Italian bourse regulator Consob.
